content.title: About
content.content: Cannellini beans are dry white beans derived from the Phaseolus vulgaris species. Originating from the Mediterranean region, they are traditionally used in soups, salads, and stews. The beans have a mild nutty flavor, a dense creamy texture when cooked, and hold their shape well, making them versatile in the kitchen.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In Italy, cannellini are often simply called “white beans” and feature in classic dishes like pasta e fagioli.
Dry beans can be stored for 2‑3 years when kept in a cool, dry place.
Soaking for 6‑12 hours before cooking reduces the cooking time and improves digestibility.
Cannellini are a popular source of plant‑based protein and fiber for vegetarian diets.
A traditional Italian preparation is “Fagioli all’uccelletto,” beans baked with olive oil, garlic, and herbs.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A 100 g serving of dry beans provides about 22 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for hemoglobin formation, while folate supports cell division and fetal development.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Cannellini raise blood glucose slowly, making them suitable for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytochemicals such as polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Dry beans contain phytates that can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and sprouting lower their levels.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Toxin risk if undercooked
items.content: Undercooked beans may retain phytohemagglutinin, causing gastrointestinal upset; always cook thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak the beans in cold water for at least 6 hours, drain, then simmer for 45‑60 minutes until tender. Use them in soups, stews, salads, purees, or as a base for vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry cannellini beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored, they remain good for 2‑3 years.
